ruling.recommended_action: Close the case: no off-route segment was measured (actual distance equals the optimal route), so no RD-2 refund arises; retain the metered fare unchanged. No account action against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider's fare complaint rests on the assumption of a longer route, but the measured record contradicts it: actual distance 8.5 km vs optimal 8.5 km, +0.0 km (-0%) [F1], and the billed distance of 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route [F3]. There is therefore no off-route segment for RD-1 to examine, and with no unexcused segment the RD-2 refund formula yields Σ(extra_km) × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km) = 0.00 km × ($11.99 ÷ 8.50 km = $1.4106/km) = $0.00, so no amount is refundable and the outcome is no_action under RD-2 [F1][F3][F5][F2][RD-2].

The extra time is fully explained by conditions rather than routing: duration 22.0 min vs estimated 16.3 min (+5.7 min) [F2], heavy rain 18.5 mm [F11], speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on both the Pan Island Expressway and Airport Boulevard during 17:09–17:47 [F8][F9]. This supports the driver's account that he followed the app route and that rain and slow traffic lengthened the trip [F7]. On a metered RydeTAXI ride the time component ($5.72 for 22.0 min) and distance component ($11.99 for 8.50 km) are chargeable as metered, and the total of $23.08 is composed of published components only: base $3.90 + distance $11.99 + time $5.72 + waiting $0.00 + platform $1.47 − discount $0.00 [F5], with no surge (1.0×) [F4]; nothing in the fare record is an unpublished add-on or an overcharge, so RD-2's non-refundable conclusion stands and no FARE-item refund is triggered [F5][F4][RD-2].

Because RD-4 is only engaged when a segment is replaced for a traffic reason, and no segment is off-route here, the traffic records [F8][F9][F10] serve only as explanation, not as a basis for exemption of any segment [F8][F10][RD-4]. The driver's prior record (1 dispute, 0 upheld) is profile material only and cannot decide anything, and since no violation of RD-1 is established, RD-6's account flag does not attach [F13][F12][RD-6]. Both briefs request no_action, consistent with the measured record [F1][F3][F6][RD-2].

SAFE-1 screen: I read the only two narrative items — the rider's complaint (a fare grievance about a longer route in heavy rain) and the driver's statement ("I followed the app route exactly. The meter is what it is; it was raining and traffic was slow."), together with the absence of any in-app chat [F6][F7]. Neither contains threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations; the complaint asserts a routing/fare issue only, so the screen is "none" with no basis facts to escalate on [F6][F7][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence status: the record settles every element this ruling needs — the distance comparison, the fare breakdown, the weather and traffic conditions and the drivers' explanation are all present [F1][F3][F5][F8][F11], and the safety screen is dispositive on the messages that exist [F6][F7]; there is accordingly no evidence gap [RD-2][SAFE-1].
